yes.why: The new site is already approved for a similar product under the same quality system, with a replicated line: a moderate change.
yes.note: For a domestic drug the production licence change comes first.

no.why: Moving drug product manufacture for a biological product is a major change: supplementary application.
no.note: For a domestic drug the production licence change comes first (Article 16).

yes.why: Moving drug product manufacture abroad for a sterile imported drug: supplementary application.

no.why: Moving drug product manufacture abroad for an imported drug: filing with CDE, with the study data the chemical guideline asks for (1 to 3 batches, 3 to 6 months of stability).
Moving drug product manufacture for a domestic drug: apply to the provincial MPA to change the production licence; after inspection and technical review the registration record is updated.
no.note: If the formulation, process or standards also change, classify those changes too.

A domestic drug substance site change goes through the production licence; the drug substance record is then updated and the formulation holders are told.

yes.why: Same address, same equipment and procedures, non-sterile step: test 1 batch and report the first batch's stability in the annual report.

no.why: A different address: validate, compare quality and impurity profile, test 3 batches: moderate change.

yes.why: The new site is already approved for a similar product under the same quality system, with a replicated line: a moderate change.
yes.note: For a domestic drug the production licence change comes first.

no.why: Moving primary packaging for a biological product is a major change: supplementary application.
no.note: For a domestic drug the production licence change comes first (Article 16).

yes.why: Moving primary packaging abroad for a sterile imported drug: supplementary application.

no.why: Moving primary packaging abroad for an imported drug: filing with CDE, with the study data the chemical guideline asks for (1 to 3 batches, 3 to 6 months of stability).
Moving primary packaging for a domestic drug: apply to the provincial MPA to change the production licence; after inspection and technical review the registration record is updated.

tree.why: A secondary packaging site: validate, test 1 batch and report in the annual report.
tree.note: A new address on a domestic production licence needs a licence change.

tree.why: A labelling site: validate, test 1 batch and report in the annual report.
tree.note: A new address on a domestic production licence needs a licence change.

yes.why: Moving a bioassay to another site is a moderate change (major if the assay uses animals).

no.why: Moving physicochemical testing: report.
The chemical guideline has no example for a testing site; holders usually classify it as a report change.

tree.why: A printing site for oral solids: validate, test 1 batch and report in the annual report.
A packaging material sterilisation site: validate, test 1 batch and report in the annual report.

yes.why: A replicated line at an approved site under the same quality system: moderate change.

no.why: A new production line for a biological product is a major change.

yes.why: A duplicate filling line with an unchanged process: moderate change with validation, including sterility assurance.

no.why: A new line that changes the process or sterility assurance: major change.

tree.why: Equipment of the same design and principle: minor change.

yes.why: Changing process steps (compounding, filling, lyophilisation) or loosening controls: major change.

no.why: A step change that does not affect critical quality: moderate change.

yes.why: A fundamental change (for example wet to dry granulation, or oven to fluid-bed drying): major change.
A change that could affect release, absorption (for example inhalation) or another critical quality attribute: major change.
A minor parameter change (for example mixing or drying time, tablet hardness with unchanged dissolution): minor change.

no.why: A process parameter or different-principle equipment change that does not affect critical quality attributes: moderate change.

yes.why: A scale change on equivalent equipment, only for batch size: moderate change.

no.why: A scale change outside those conditions: major change.

yes.why: A batch size change for a special dosage form (complex modified release, enteric, transdermal, liposome, long-acting): major change.
A batch size change for an aseptically made product with longer sterility-relevant steps: moderate change.
Within ten times the pivotal clinical or bioequivalence batch (oral solids and non-sterile semisolids): minor change.

no.why: More than ten times the pivotal batch: moderate change.

tree.why: A new route of synthesis: major change.

yes.why: A change from the final step onward, or one that could change the impurity profile or key physicochemical properties: major change.
New or tighter in-process controls, a higher grade of reagent or solvent, or equipment before the final step: minor change.

no.why: Reagents, solvents or conditions before the final step changed with the same impurity profile: moderate change.

tree.why: Extending the route so the old starting material becomes an intermediate: moderate change.
Adding a reprocessing procedure to the registered process: major change.
tree.note: Making an existing rework a fixed step is moderate.

yes.why: An ink of components already used in approved drugs: minor change.

no.why: Another ink is a moderate change.

yes.why: A marking change on a modified-release product: major change.

no.why: A non-functional marking change on an oral solid: minor change.

yes.why: A change in the order of operations is a moderate change (not for vaccine liquid formulations).

no.why: Changing the order of adding components (not the drug substance) to a solution: minor change.

yes.why: Changing the sterilising filter pore size: major change.

no.why: Filtration parameters beyond the approved range (same pore size), or one filter replaced by two in series: moderate change.

tree.why: Changing the sterilisation method (filtration and terminal sterilisation, overkill and bioburden-based, dry heat and radiation): major change.

yes.why: A change that could affect sterility assurance: major change.

no.why: A depyrogenation change with equivalent assurance: moderate change.

yes.why: Removing a filtration in an aseptic process: major change.

no.why: Removing an intermediate filtration in a terminally sterilised product: moderate change.

yes.why: A control added because of a process defect or stability problem is a major change.

no.why: Adding an in-process control or tightening one: minor change.

yes.why: Changing the excipient composition or concentration of a biological product: major change.

minor.why: An excipient amount change within the minor limits (for oral solids, each excipient and the total within 5 percent, unit weight unchanged): minor change.

moderate.why: An excipient amount change beyond the minor limits but within the moderate ones (total within 10 percent, unit weight within 10 percent), or a change of excipient grade: moderate change.

major.why: An excipient amount change beyond the moderate limits, a narrow therapeutic index or BCS class IV drug beyond the minor limits, or a change in excipient type: major change.

tree.why: Removing or reducing a colourant or flavour: minor change.
Every new strength is a major change: supplementary application, within the approved dosing range.

yes.why: Tightening a drug substance limit: moderate change.

no.why: Tightening a drug product limit: minor change.
Tightening a limit within the approved range: moderate change.

tree.why: Relaxing a limit is a major change.

yes.why: Deleting a test is a major change.

no.why: Deleting a redundant test when the product is unchanged: minor change.
Deleting any item from the registered specification is a major change.

yes.why: Adding a drug substance test with a limit: moderate change.

no.why: Adding a drug product test: minor change.
Adding a test that is not needed for safety or because of a process change: moderate change.

tree.why: Updating the registration standard to a revised national standard (Chinese Pharmacopoeia): file or report as the guidelines say; usually a moderate change.

yes.why: A method change with the same principle, or equal or better performance: moderate change.

no.why: Replacing an analytical method: major change.
Changing a test method in the registered specification is a major change.

yes.why: A new method with equal or better performance: moderate change.

no.why: A new method principle: major change.
A new method in the registered specification is a major change.

yes.why: An alternative method with equal or better performance: moderate change.

no.why: Replacing an analytical method: major change.
Adding or deleting a method in the registered specification is a major change.

tree.why: Changing an analytical method for in-process or component control without lowering control: moderate change.
Changing the standard or grade of reagents or solvents without lowering quality: minor change.

yes.why: A change in direct-contact packaging material is a major change.
A material or type change for an injection, inhalation or ophthalmic container: major change.

no.why: A material or type change for a liquid or semisolid container (not injection, inhalation or ophthalmic): moderate change.

yes.why: A change in direct-contact material, shape or size: major change.

no.why: A new supplier of the same component, approved or with status A: minor change.

yes.why: A material or type change for an injection container: major change.

no.why: A new supplier, size or shape of an injection container: moderate change.

tree.why: A change in supplier, size or shape of a metered-dose device: major change.

yes.why: Changing the type of packaging for a non-sterile solid (blister, bottle, bag): moderate change.

no.why: A supplier, size or shape change, or a material already used for the same route with equal or better performance: minor change.

tree.why: A material or type change for a non-sterile liquid: moderate change.

yes.why: A shape or size change with different internal dimensions: major change.

no.why: A shape or size change with equivalent internal dimensions and the same material: minor change.

yes.why: A size or shape change of an injection container: moderate change.

no.why: A size or shape change not otherwise listed: minor change.

yes.why: A pack size change: minor change.
A count change for unit-dose packs (tablets per blister, vials per box): minor change.

no.why: A count change for multi-dose packs (tablets per bottle, grams per tube): moderate change.

tree.why: Adding, changing or removing a desiccant changes the protection: moderate change.

yes.why: A blister type change (for example alu-alu to alu-PVC): moderate change.

no.why: A blister supplier, size or shape change: minor change.

tree.why: Removing secondary packaging that gives extra protection: major change.
A non-contact packaging change that does not affect stability, transport or safety: minor change.

yes.why: Extending the shelf life on at least three commercial batches under the approved stability protocol: moderate change.

no.why: Extending the shelf life on other data: major change.
Extending the shelf life within the long-term stability data already completed: moderate change.

yes.why: Shortening the shelf life because of a manufacturing or stability problem is a major change.

no.why: Shortening the shelf life for other reasons: moderate change.

yes.why: A tighter stability protocol (for example more time points): minor change.

no.why: Another stability protocol change: moderate change.
The chemical guideline has no example; a protocol change is usually filed.

yes.why: Tightening the storage conditions within the approved range: minor change.

no.why: Relaxing the storage conditions: major change.
Changing the storage conditions is a major change.

yes.why: A new reference lot confirmed under the approved protocol: minor change.

no.why: A new reference lot confirmed against an approved reference, or a new protocol: moderate change.
The chemical guideline has no example; a new working standard qualified against the primary standard is usually a report change.

tree.why: A new indication changes efficacy content of the package insert: supplementary application.
Changing the population or dosage changes efficacy content: supplementary application.
Clinical study results are efficacy content of the package insert: supplementary application.
Adding or strengthening safety information does not increase risk, so it is filed.
tree.note: A change that weakens safety information increases risk and needs approval.

yes.why: An instruction about dosage and administration touches efficacy content or could increase safety risk: supplementary application.

no.why: An instruction about dosage and administration: a package insert change that does not touch efficacy content and does not increase risk is filed.

yes.why: Deleting unsupported text touches efficacy content or could increase safety risk: supplementary application.

no.why: Deleting unsupported text: a package insert change that does not touch efficacy content and does not increase risk is filed.

tree.why: When NMPA announces a unified revision of package inserts, each holder files its revised insert by the date in the announcement.

yes.why: Aligning a generic's package insert with the reference drug touches efficacy content or could increase safety risk: supplementary application.

no.why: Aligning a generic's package insert with the reference drug: a package insert change that does not touch efficacy content and does not increase risk is filed.

tree.why: An editorial change to the package insert or labels is filed.
A change to the content or layout of package labels is a filing change (Article 79).
China has no post-approval change management protocol route in force; CDE consulted on a draft guideline for chemical drugs in 2025.
There is no approved protocol route yet; classify the change itself in its own entry.
A change that needs a bioequivalence study is a major change.

yes.why: A new master cell bank from the original or an approved master bank, prepared the same way with the same or tighter specifications: moderate change.

no.why: A master cell bank not derived from the original or an approved master bank, or a new expression vector: major change.

yes.why: A new working cell bank from an approved master bank within the approved passage limit: moderate change.

no.why: A working cell bank outside those conditions: major change.

yes.why: A critical change (for example one that affects virus clearance or the impurity profile): major change.
A non-critical change that also meets the stricter conditions: minor change.

no.why: A non-critical change with no new impurity and no effect on virus clearance: moderate change.

yes.why: A change that significantly affects virus clearance is a major change.

no.why: Another change to a virus inactivation or removal step: moderate, with its own validation.

tree.why: Transferring the marketing authorisation is a supplementary application to CDE; for a domestic transfer, the new holder first gets a production licence.
A change in the holder's name or registered address name: for a domestic holder, change the licence first, then file; for an imported drug, file with CDE.

yes.why: Switching to a drug substance that is already approved (status A on the registration platform): moderate change.
yes.note: If dissolution or key properties of the product differ, a bioequivalence study may be needed.

no.why: Switching to a drug substance that is not yet approved: major change.

tree.why: The holder releases batches under GMP; a new quality control laboratory is usually a report change.
Removing a supplier or site: minor change.
tree.note: A domestic production licence is updated if an address goes.

yes.why: Within ten times the approved drug substance batch: minor change.

no.why: More than ten times the approved batch: moderate change.

tree.why: Tightening an in-process limit: minor change.

yes.why: Relaxing a control range with supporting data: moderate change.

no.why: Relaxing or deleting an approved control is a major change.

yes.why: A longer hold with supporting data: moderate change.
A bulk solution hold more than 50 percent longer (terminally sterilised): moderate change.

no.why: A bulk solution hold up to 50 percent longer with the same bioburden: minor change.

tree.why: Working within an approved design space is not a change.
Establishing or expanding a design space is a major change.
Using a design space for parametric or real-time release is a major change.
Converting to continuous manufacturing is a fundamental process change: major change.

yes.why: A simple, stable excipient (for example an inorganic salt or sucrose) from a new supplier with status A: minor change.

no.why: A new excipient supplier that is approved or registered with status A: moderate change.
A new supplier of the same grade with no lower quality: minor change.

minor.why: A coating or shell weight change within the minor limits (for oral solids, each excipient and the total within 5 percent, unit weight unchanged): minor change.

moderate.why: A coating or shell weight change beyond the minor limits but within the moderate ones (total within 10 percent, unit weight within 10 percent), or a change of excipient grade: moderate change.

major.why: A coating or shell weight change beyond the moderate limits, a narrow therapeutic index or BCS class IV drug beyond the minor limits, or a change in excipient type: major change.

tree.why: Adding or deleting a functional score line: major change.

yes.why: A shape or size change of a modified-release product: major change.
A significant shape change (for example round to an irregular shape) with unchanged dissolution: moderate change.

no.why: A slight shape or size adjustment with unchanged dissolution: minor change.

yes.why: Replacing an animal-derived material with a non-animal one: moderate change.

no.why: Replacing an excipient of animal origin with the same excipient of another origin is a moderate change.

tree.why: A new dosage form is a new registration (an improved new drug or a generic of that form).
Adding a test and limit is a moderate change.

tighten.why: Raising an excipient standard: minor change.

add.why: Adding an excipient test raises the standard: minor change.

delete.why: Deleting an excipient test lowers control: major change.

relax.why: Relaxing an excipient standard lowers control: major change.

yes.why: Moving routine testing into in-process control under approved conditions: moderate change.

no.why: Testing less than every batch removes an item from routine release: major change.

yes.why: A minor method change with equal or better performance: minor change.

no.why: An adjustment within the approved method is filed when it changes the registered text.

yes.why: An equal-or-better method: moderate change.

no.why: Replacing a method: major change.
Changing a test method in the registered specification is a major change.

yes.why: A new supplier of a direct-contact item, approved or with status A: minor change.
A new supplier of an injection container: moderate change.

no.why: A new supplier not otherwise listed: minor change.

yes.why: A device change that could change the dose delivered: major change.

no.why: A measuring or administration device supplied with the product: moderate change.

tree.why: A non-contact packaging part that does not affect stability, transport or safety: minor change.
Extending the drug substance re-test period within completed long-term data: moderate change.
Changing the storage after reconstitution or dilution: moderate change.

yes.why: Tightening drug substance storage conditions: moderate change.

no.why: Changing the storage conditions is a major change.

tree.why: A new route of administration is a new registration.
A trade name change needs a supplementary application.
China has no separate filing for a risk management plan update; the plan is kept in the pharmacovigilance system and summarised in periodic safety reports.

yes.why: Safety wording after a periodic safety report or signal assessment touches efficacy content or could increase safety risk: supplementary application.

no.why: Safety wording after a periodic safety report or signal assessment: a package insert change that does not touch efficacy content and does not increase risk is filed.

tree.why: Deleting an indication changes efficacy content: supplementary application.
Established conditions are not part of the Chinese change rules yet; the registration dossier and the holder's change list play that role.
China does not use a PLCM document.
Without established conditions, the change is classified by the technical guidelines: see its own entry.
There is no approved protocol route yet.

yes.why: A culture scale change on the same bioreactor type with linear scaling within approved ranges: moderate change.

no.why: A scale change outside those conditions: major change.

key.why: Adding, removing or replacing a key medium component, or changing the source of an animal-derived material: major change.

keyNoImpact.why: A key component change with no effect on key quality attributes, or replacing an animal-derived material with a non-animal one: moderate change.

nonkey.why: A non-key component change: minor change.

lifetime.why: Extending the resin lifetime is a non-critical purification change: moderate change.

yes.why: A different resin that could affect clearance or impurities: major change.

no.why: An equivalent resin from another supplier: moderate change.

yes.why: A potency assay with a new principle is a major change.

no.why: A potency method change with the same principle, equal or better: moderate change.

tree.why: A change in excipient composition or concentration, or removing an excipient, is a major change.

first.why: New viral safety claims need the purification and clearance data reviewed: major change.

higher.why: A higher-risk evaluation is a major change.

same.why: Updated data with the same risk: moderate change.

tree.why: A change in the manufacturer's name or address name (no move) is filed, after the licence change for a domestic manufacturer.
Changing the domestic agent named by an overseas holder is filed with CDE.
Changing the common name to a new national name is filed.

strength.why: Each strength has its own approval number: apply to cancel that registration certificate.

pack.why: Removing a pack size: minor change.
